# What this document does

SEIR v2 (`SEIR_BiLSTM.Rmd`) estimates R0 very well on simulated epidemics, but real
data differ from its training curves. v4 keeps v2's structure (61 days; known `n`,
`recov`, `incub`; tuned settings; average of several seeds) and changes the training
data and outputs:

| | SEIR v2 | SEIR v4 and v5 |
|---|---|---|
| Training curves | every new case, smooth | **reported cases**: a share of the cases, weekday swings and extra day-to-day noise |
| Share initially exposed | 1% to 40% | **0.1% to 40%** (log scale) |
| Incubation days | 3 to 21 | **1 to 21** (flu is about 2) |
| R0 | 1 to 5 | **0.8 to 5** (declining epidemics too) |
| Network input | cases / 10,000 | **log(1 + cases) / log(1 + 10,000)**, so small counts are readable |
| Outputs | ptran, crate, R0, preval | ptran, R0, preval, **reported share, noise, weekday swing**; **no crate** |
| Result | one value per parameter | one value **plus a range for R0** and fit bands that include it |

Why these changes:

- **Reported cases.** Real data count only some infections (flu data here are hospital
  admissions), have weekday patterns and reporting spikes. The noise ranges come from the
  real datasets: weekday swings of 15-25% and extra noise (overdispersion) up to about 0.2.
- **No crate output.** Only R0 = ptran x crate / recov can be read from a curve; crate
  was about 90% of v2's training loss and its value was replaced anyway. `crate` is still
  returned, computed from R0, ptran and recov as before.
- **Prior immunity is left out on purpose**: a population with 30% immune behaves like a
  smaller population with a lower R0, so it cannot be told apart from R0 in the data.
- **A range for R0.** The network gives one value. A separate calibration bank of
  `r format(params$n_calib, big.mark = ",")` simulated epidemics shows how far the true
  values fall from the network's estimate for similar curves (the
  `r params$k_neighbors` most similar estimates); those errors give the range, and
  simulated curves drawn from it give fit bands that include the uncertainty in R0.
  This is checked on new simulated epidemics: a 95% range should hold the true R0 about
  95% of the time.
- **New noise every epoch** (`fresh_noise: true`, used for v5). v4 trained on one fixed
  noisy copy of each curve and started to learn that noise by heart after about 25
  epochs. With `fresh_noise` the training bank holds the true daily cases, and the
  trainer draws new reported cases (same reporting model) for every batch, so the network
  never sees the same noise twice. The test and calibration curves are the same as v4's.

This run: **SEIR `r params$model_name`**`r if (isTRUE(params$fresh_noise)) ", new noise every epoch" else ""``r if (params$hidden_size > 0) paste0(", ", params$hidden_size, " hidden units") else ""`.

To run it (from the `examples/` folder):

```r
rmarkdown::render("SEIR_v4_BiLSTM.Rmd", output_dir = "results/seir_bilstm_v4")
```

```{r settings}
N_SIMS    <- params$n_sims
N_DAYS    <- params$n_days
EPOCHS    <- params$epochs
N_TEST    <- params$n_test
N_CALIB   <- params$n_calib
N_REPS    <- params$n_reps
K_NB      <- params$k_neighbors
MIN_CASES <- params$min_cases
RETRAIN   <- isTRUE(params$retrain)
OUT_DIR   <- params$out_dir
SIM_CORES <- as.integer(params$sim_cores)
SEEDS     <- as.integer(params$seeds)
ENSEMBLE  <- isTRUE(params$ensemble) && length(SEEDS) > 1
MODEL       <- paste("SEIR", params$model_name)
FRESH_NOISE <- isTRUE(params$fresh_noise)
BAND_ONE    <- paste0(params$model_name, ", one estimate")
BAND_RANGE  <- paste0(params$model_name, ", with range")

BANK_SEED  <- 122
TEST_SEED  <- 2025   # different seeds: no test or calibration curve is seen in training
CALIB_SEED <- 7

KNOWN   <- c("n", "recov", "incub")
TARGETS <- c("ptran", "R0", "log_preval", "log_report_rate", "log_overdispersion", "weekday_sd")
OUTPUT_ACTIVATION   <- c("sigmoid", "softplus", "sigmoid", "sigmoid", "sigmoid", "sigmoid")
INCIDENCE_MAX       <- 10000
INCIDENCE_TRANSFORM <- "log1p"

PRIORS <- list(
  n = c(5000, 10000), recov = c(0.071, 0.25), crate = c(5, 15), incub = c(1, 21),
  R0 = c(0.8, 5), preval = c(0.001, 0.4),
  report_rate = c(0.05, 1), overdispersion = c(0.001, 0.3), weekday_sd = c(0, 0.35)
)
# What v2 was trained on (100 to 2,000 initially exposed out of 5,000 to 10,000).
in_v2_range <- function(theta) theta$incub >= 3 & theta$R0 >= 1 & theta$preval >= 0.01

# Tuned v2 settings. The physics penalty needs a crate output, so it is off.
hp <- jsonlite::read_json(params$hyperparameters)
LEARNING_RATE  <- hp$learning_rate
BATCH_SIZE     <- as.integer(hp$batch_size)
HIDDEN_SIZE    <- as.integer(hp$hidden_size)
NUM_LAYERS     <- as.integer(hp$num_layers)
DROPOUT        <- hp$dropout
PHYSICS_WEIGHT <- 0
GRAD_CLIP      <- params$grad_clip
if (params$hidden_size > 0) HIDDEN_SIZE <- as.integer(params$hidden_size)

V2_DIRS <- trimws(strsplit(params$v2_models, ",")[[1]])

dir.create(OUT_DIR, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.path = file.path(normalizePath(OUT_DIR), "figures", ""))

prior_text <- vapply(names(PRIORS), function(p) paste(signif(PRIORS[[p]], 3), collapse = " to "), "")
settings <- data.frame(
  setting = c("training simulations", "days per curve", "epochs", "test curves",
              "calibration curves (for the R0 range)", "most similar curves used for the range",
              "fit simulations per band", "curves kept if reported cases at least",
              paste("range of", names(PRIORS)),
              "learning rate", "batch size", "hidden units", "BiLSTM layers", "dropout",
              "gradient clipping", "network input", "new reporting noise every batch",
              "network seeds", "output folder"),
  value = c(N_SIMS, N_DAYS, EPOCHS, N_TEST, N_CALIB, K_NB, N_REPS, MIN_CASES, prior_text,
            signif(LEARNING_RATE, 3), BATCH_SIZE, HIDDEN_SIZE, NUM_LAYERS, round(DROPOUT, 3),
            GRAD_CLIP, sprintf("log(1 + cases) / log(1 + %d)", INCIDENCE_MAX),
            if (FRESH_NOISE) "yes" else "no", paste(SEEDS, collapse = ", "), normalizePath(OUT_DIR))
)
write.csv(settings, file.path(OUT_DIR, "settings.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(settings)
```

`preval`, `report_rate` and `overdispersion` are drawn on the log scale and estimated on
the log scale (`log_` targets; the calibrator returns them on the normal scale).

# Step 1: simulate the banks

Three banks from the same simulator with different seeds: training, test and calibration.
Epidemics with fewer than `r MIN_CASES` reported cases in `r N_DAYS` days (nothing to
learn from, and never what one would calibrate) are dropped; 15% extra are simulated to
make up for them. With `sim_cores` above 1 a bank is simulated in that many chunks at
once; chunk `k` uses seed `seed + k - 1`. With `fresh_noise` the training bank holds the
true daily cases (the reporting parameters are drawn and saved, but applied by the
trainer), and a curve is kept when its expected number of reported cases is at least
`r MIN_CASES`.

```{r banks}
simulate_bank <- function(n_keep, seed, true_cases = FALSE) {
  n_draw <- ceiling(1.15 * n_keep)
  sim_chunk <- function(size, s) {
    base <- seir_simulator(ndays = N_DAYS, priors = PRIORS)
    sim  <- if (!true_cases) base else new_simulator(base$sample_parameters, function(parameters, seed) {
      parameters$report_rate <- NULL   # true cases; the trainer draws the reported ones
      base$run(parameters, seed)
    }, type = "SEIR")
    simulate_training_data(sim, n_sims = size, seed = s)
  }
  if (SIM_CORES > 1) {
    sizes  <- diff(round(seq(0, n_draw, length.out = SIM_CORES + 1)))
    chunks <- parallel::mclapply(seq_along(sizes), function(k) sim_chunk(sizes[k], seed + k - 1),
                                 mc.cores = SIM_CORES)
    failed <- vapply(chunks, inherits, logical(1), what = "try-error")
    if (any(failed)) stop("Simulation chunk(s) failed: ", paste(which(failed), collapse = ", "))
    theta <- do.call(rbind, lapply(chunks, `[[`, "theta"))
    obs   <- do.call(rbind, lapply(chunks, `[[`, "observations"))
  } else {
    b <- sim_chunk(n_draw, seed)
    theta <- b$theta
    obs   <- b$observations
  }
  reported <- if (true_cases) theta$report_rate * rowSums(obs) else rowSums(obs)
  keep <- which(reported >= MIN_CASES)
  if (length(keep) < n_keep) stop("Only ", length(keep), " curves with enough cases; simulate more.")
  keep <- keep[seq_len(n_keep)]
  theta <- theta[keep, ]
  for (v in c("preval", "report_rate", "overdispersion")) theta[[paste0("log_", v)]] <- log(theta[[v]])
  rownames(theta) <- NULL
  bank <- new_training_data(theta, obs[keep, ], type = "SEIR",
                            source = "epiworldR ModelSEIRCONN with reporting")
  attr(bank, "dropped_share") <- mean(reported < MIN_CASES)
  bank
}

bank_files <- function(dir) file.path(dir, c("seir_theta.csv", "seir_observations.csv"))

load_or_simulate <- function(name, n_keep, seed, true_cases = FALSE) {
  dir   <- file.path(OUT_DIR, name)
  files <- bank_files(dir)
  if (all(file.exists(files)) && nrow(data.table::fread(files[1], select = 1L)) == n_keep) {
    return(list(bank = read_training_data(files[1], files[2], type = "SEIR"), fresh = FALSE))
  }
  t <- system.time(bank <- simulate_bank(n_keep, seed, true_cases))
  save_training_data(bank, name = "seir", output_dir = dir)
  writeLines(as.character(c(round(t[["elapsed"]]), attr(bank, "dropped_share"))),
             file.path(dir, "simulation_seconds_and_dropped_share.txt"))
  list(bank = bank, fresh = TRUE)
}

x <- load_or_simulate("training_bank", N_SIMS, BANK_SEED, true_cases = FRESH_NOISE)
train_bank <- x$bank
fresh_bank <- x$fresh
test_bank  <- load_or_simulate("test_bank", N_TEST, TEST_SEED)$bank
calib_bank <- load_or_simulate("calibration_bank", N_CALIB, CALIB_SEED)$bank
theta_file <- bank_files(file.path(OUT_DIR, "training_bank"))[1]
obs_file   <- bank_files(file.path(OUT_DIR, "training_bank"))[2]

info <- readLines(file.path(OUT_DIR, "training_bank", "simulation_seconds_and_dropped_share.txt"))
cat("Training bank:", format(nrow(train_bank$theta), big.mark = ","), "curves | simulated in",
    round(as.numeric(info[1]) / 60, 1), "minutes |", sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * as.numeric(info[2])),
    "dropped for too few cases\n")
summary(train_bank$theta[, c(KNOWN, "R0", "preval", "report_rate", "overdispersion", "weekday_sd")])
```

```{r example-curves, fig.width=11, fig.height=5}
for (i in sample(nrow(test_bank$theta), 8)) {

  plot(test_bank$observations[i, ], type = "h", col = "blue", xlab = "day", ylab = "reported cases",
       main = sprintf("R0 %.1f, %.0f%% reported\nnoise %.2f, weekday %.2f", th$R0, 100 * th$report_rate,
```

# Step 2: train and save the model

One model per seed, each in its own folder. A model is retrained when `retrain: true`,
when the training bank was just simulated, or when the saved model used other settings.

```{r train}
model_dirs <- file.path(OUT_DIR, paste0("model_seed_", SEEDS))

model_matches <- function(dir, seed) {
  config_file <- file.path(dir, "model_config.json")
  if (!file.exists(file.path(dir, "model.pt")) || !file.exists(config_file)) return(FALSE)
  cfg <- jsonlite::read_json(config_file)
  cfg$epochs == EPOCHS && cfg$seed == seed &&
    identical(unlist(cfg$known_names), KNOWN) &&
    identical(unlist(cfg$target_names), TARGETS) &&
    cfg$batch_size == BATCH_SIZE && cfg$hidden_size == HIDDEN_SIZE &&
    cfg$num_layers == NUM_LAYERS && isTRUE(all.equal(cfg$dropout, DROPOUT)) &&
    isTRUE(all.equal(cfg$learning_rate, LEARNING_RATE)) &&
    isTRUE(all.equal(cfg$incidence_max, INCIDENCE_MAX)) &&
    identical(cfg$incidence_transform, INCIDENCE_TRANSFORM) &&
    identical(isTRUE(cfg$observation_noise), FRESH_NOISE) &&
    isTRUE(all.equal(cfg$grad_clip, GRAD_CLIP)) &&
    identical(unlist(cfg$output_activations), OUTPUT_ACTIVATION)
}

for (i in seq_along(SEEDS)) {
  if (RETRAIN || fresh_bank || !model_matches(model_dirs[i], SEEDS[i])) {
    t <- system.time(train_bilstm_calibrator(
      name = "seir", known_names = KNOWN, target_names = TARGETS, type = "SEIR",
      parameter_file = theta_file, observation_file = obs_file, output_dir = model_dirs[i],
      epochs = EPOCHS, batch_size = BATCH_SIZE, learning_rate = LEARNING_RATE, seed = SEEDS[i],
      hidden_size = HIDDEN_SIZE, num_layers = NUM_LAYERS, dropout = DROPOUT,
      physics_weight = PHYSICS_WEIGHT, incidence_max = INCIDENCE_MAX,
      incidence_transform = INCIDENCE_TRANSFORM, output_activation = OUTPUT_ACTIVATION,
      grad_clip = GRAD_CLIP, device = params$device, observation_noise = FRESH_NOISE
    ))
    writeLines(as.character(round(t[["elapsed"]])), file.path(model_dirs[i], "training_seconds.txt"))
  }
}

train_info <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(SEEDS), function(i) {
  cfg <- jsonlite::read_json(file.path(model_dirs[i], "model_config.json"))
  data.frame(seed = SEEDS[i], best_epoch = cfg$best_epoch, trained_on = cfg$device,
             minutes = round(as.numeric(readLines(file.path(model_dirs[i], "training_seconds.txt"))) / 60, 1))
}))
knitr::kable(train_info, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r stop-after-training, include=FALSE}

```

Validation loss by target (0-1 scale) for each seed. A seed whose loss stays flat
would be a failed run.

```{r history, fig.width=11, fig.height=4}
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
for (what in c("validation_loss", "validation_mse_R0", "validation_mse_log_report_rate")) {
  h <- lapply(model_dirs, function(d) read.csv(file.path(d, "training_history.csv")))
  plot(NA, xlim = c(1, EPOCHS), ylim = range(unlist(lapply(h, `[[`, what))), log = "y",
       xlab = "epoch", ylab = what, main = what)
  for (k in seq_along(h)) lines(h[[k]]$epoch, h[[k]][[what]], col = k, lwd = 1.5)
  legend("topright", bty = "n", lwd = 1.5, col = seq_along(h), legend = paste("seed", SEEDS))
}
par(op)
```

# Step 3: new simulated epidemics

Estimates for many curves at once (the same numbers as `calibrate()`, checked below).
With several seeds the main model is their average; `crate` is computed from the averaged
R0 and ptran, as in v2.

```{r predict-helpers}
predict_models <- function(dirs, curves, known) {
  curves <- as.matrix(curves)
  known  <- as.data.frame(known)[, KNOWN, drop = FALSE]
  ests <- lapply(dirs, function(d) bilstm_predict_many(d, curves, known, device = params$device))
  avg  <- Reduce(`+`, ests) / length(ests)
  avg$crate <- avg$R0 * known$recov / avg$ptran
  avg
}
MODEL_DIRS <- if (ENSEMBLE) model_dirs else model_dirs[1]
MODEL_LABEL <- if (ENSEMBLE) sprintf("%s (average of %d seeds)", MODEL, length(SEEDS)) else MODEL
V2_LABEL <- sprintf("SEIR v2 (average of %d seeds)", length(V2_DIRS))

# The fast path gives the same numbers as calibrate().
cal_model <- bilstm_calibrator(model_dirs[1], known_names = KNOWN, type = "SEIR", device = params$device)
one  <- t(vapply(1:3, function(i) calibrate(test_bank$observations[i, ], cal_model, n = test_bank$theta$n[i],
              recov = test_bank$theta$recov[i], incub = test_bank$theta$incub[i])[c("ptran", "R0", "preval", "crate")],
              numeric(4)))
many <- predict_models(model_dirs[1], test_bank$observations[1:3, ], test_bank$theta[1:3, ])
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(unname(as.matrix(many[, c("ptran", "R0", "preval", "crate")])), unname(one),
                           tolerance = 1e-5)))
```

```{r test-predict}
v2_test <- read_training_data(file.path(params$v2_test_dir, "seir_theta.csv"),
                              file.path(params$v2_test_dir, "seir_observations.csv"), type = "SEIR")
est <- list(
  noisy = list(v2 = predict_models(V2_DIRS, test_bank$observations, test_bank$theta),
               model = predict_models(MODEL_DIRS, test_bank$observations, test_bank$theta)),
  clean = list(v2 = predict_models(V2_DIRS, v2_test$observations, v2_test$theta),
               model = predict_models(MODEL_DIRS, v2_test$observations, v2_test$theta))
)
r0_score <- function(e, t) c(R0_MAE = mean(abs(e - t)), R0_R2 = 1 - sum((e - t)^2) / sum((t - mean(t))^2))
inside <- in_v2_range(test_bank$theta)
rows <- list(
  list("New test bank (reported cases), all curves", "noisy", rep(TRUE, N_TEST)),
  list("New test bank, inside v2's training range", "noisy", inside),
  list("New test bank, outside v2's training range", "noisy", !inside),
  list("v2's test bank (every case, smooth)", "clean", rep(TRUE, nrow(v2_test$theta)))
)
test_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(rows, function(r) {
  truth <- if (r[[2]] == "noisy") test_bank$theta$R0 else v2_test$theta$R0
  s2 <- r0_score(est[[r[[2]]]]$v2$R0[r[[3]]], truth[r[[3]]])
  s4 <- r0_score(est[[r[[2]]]]$model$R0[r[[3]]], truth[r[[3]]])
  data.frame(test_curves = r[[1]], n = sum(r[[3]]),
             v2_R0_MAE = s2[["R0_MAE"]], model_R0_MAE = s4[["R0_MAE"]],
             v2_R0_R2 = s2[["R0_R2"]], model_R0_R2 = s4[["R0_R2"]])
}))
write.csv(test_tab, file.path(OUT_DIR, "test_R0_v2_vs_model.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(test_tab, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r test-scatter, fig.width=11, fig.height=4}

op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))

abline(0, 1, lty = 2)
par(op)
```

The other outputs on the new test bank (`R2` on the scale the network learns: log
for preval, reported share and noise):

```{r test-other-targets}
truth <- test_bank$theta
e4 <- est$noisy$model
other <- data.frame(
  output = c("R0", "ptran", "log preval", "log reported share", "log noise (overdispersion)", "weekday swing"),
  truth  = I(list(truth$R0, truth$ptran, log(truth$preval), log(truth$report_rate),
                  log(truth$overdispersion), truth$weekday_sd)),
  est    = I(list(e4$R0, e4$ptran, log(e4$preval), log(e4$report_rate), log(e4$overdispersion), e4$weekday_sd))
)
other_tab <- data.frame(
  output = other$output,
  MAE = mapply(function(t, e) mean(abs(e - t)), other$truth, other$est),
  R2  = mapply(function(t, e) 1 - sum((e - t)^2) / sum((t - mean(t))^2), other$truth, other$est)
)
write.csv(other_tab, file.path(OUT_DIR, "test_all_outputs.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(other_tab, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

# Step 4: a range for R0

For each curve: its estimates, together with the known `recov` and `incub`, are
compared with the estimates for the `r format(N_CALIB, big.mark = ",")` calibration
curves; for the `r K_NB` most similar ones, the differences between true and estimated
values are added to the curve's estimate. That gives the R0 range and, for the fit
bands, `r N_REPS` parameter draws.

```{r calibration}
calib_est <- predict_models(MODEL_DIRS, calib_bank$observations, calib_bank$theta)
features <- function(e, known) cbind(R0 = e$R0, lp = log(e$preval), lr = log(e$report_rate),
                                     lo = log(e$overdispersion), recov = known$recov, incub = known$incub)
F_cal  <- features(calib_est, calib_bank$theta)
F_mean <- colMeans(F_cal)
F_sd   <- apply(F_cal, 2, sd)
F_cal_t <- t(scale(F_cal, F_mean, F_sd))
th <- calib_bank$theta
resid_cal <- data.frame(
  R0 = th$R0 - calib_est$R0, lp = log(th$preval) - log(calib_est$preval),
  lr = log(th$report_rate) - log(calib_est$report_rate),
  lo = log(th$overdispersion) - log(calib_est$overdispersion), wsd = th$weekday_sd - calib_est$weekday_sd
)

neighbours <- function(e, known) {
  f <- (features(e, known)[1, ] - F_mean) / F_sd
  d <- colSums((F_cal_t - f)^2)
  which(d <= sort(d, partial = K_NB)[K_NB])[seq_len(K_NB)]
}
r0_range <- function(e, nb, probs) e$R0 + quantile(resid_cal$R0[nb], probs, names = FALSE)

# Parameter draws for one curve: its estimate plus the errors of similar curves.
draw_parameters <- function(e, known, nb, n_draws) {
  j <- sample(nb, n_draws, replace = TRUE)
  R0 <- pmax(0.05, e$R0 + resid_cal$R0[j])
  data.frame(
    n = known$n, recov = known$recov, incub = known$incub,
    preval = pmin(0.9, exp(log(e$preval) + resid_cal$lp[j])),
    ptran = e$ptran, crate = R0 * known$recov / e$ptran,
    report_rate = pmin(1, exp(log(e$report_rate) + resid_cal$lr[j])),
    overdispersion = exp(log(e$overdispersion) + resid_cal$lo[j]),
    weekday_sd = pmax(0, e$weekday_sd + resid_cal$wsd[j])
  )
}

ranges <- t(vapply(seq_len(N_TEST), function(i) {
  e  <- est$noisy$model[i, ]
  nb <- neighbours(e, test_bank$theta[i, ])
  r0_range(e, nb, c(0.025, 0.975, 0.25, 0.75))
}, numeric(4)))
t0 <- test_bank$theta$R0
range_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(list(list("all test curves", rep(TRUE, N_TEST)),
                                         list("inside v2's training range", inside),
                                         list("outside v2's training range", !inside)), function(r) {
  s <- r[[2]]
  data.frame(test_curves = r[[1]], n = sum(s),
             in_95_range_pct = 100 * mean(t0[s] >= ranges[s, 1] & t0[s] <= ranges[s, 2]),
             in_50_range_pct = 100 * mean(t0[s] >= ranges[s, 3] & t0[s] <= ranges[s, 4]),
             mean_width_95 = mean(ranges[s, 2] - ranges[s, 1]))
}))
write.csv(range_tab, file.path(OUT_DIR, "R0_range_check.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(range_tab, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Share of test curves whose true R0 is inside the range (should be about 95% and 50%)")
```

```{r range-plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=4.5}
s <- order(t0)[round(seq(1, N_TEST, length.out = 80))]
plot(seq_along(s), t0[s], pch = 16, col = "blue", ylim = range(ranges[s, 1:2]), xlab = "test curve (by true R0)",
     ylab = "R0", main = "95% range (grey) and estimate (purple) for 80 test curves; true R0 in blue")
segments(seq_along(s), ranges[s, 1], seq_along(s), ranges[s, 2], col = "grey50", lwd = 2)
points(seq_along(s), est$noisy$model$R0[s], pch = 3, col = "purple")
```

# Step 5: real data

The same datasets as `Test_SEIR_real_data.Rmd` and the Utah windows of
`Compare_SEIR_v2_v3_windows.Rmd`:

- **Utah COVID-19 2024-25**: 61-day windows starting every 14 days over the last 365 days
  (beginning, middle and end included); `n = 5000`, `recov = 1/7`, `incub = `r params$utah_incub``.
- **Utah flu 2022-23 and 2023-24** (daily hospital admissions), **Baltimore flu 1918**
  and **Utah COVID-19 summer 2023**: the 61 days ending a week after the peak.
  Flu: `recov = 0.25`, `incub = `r params$flu_incub`` for `r params$model_name`; v2 cannot go below 3 days, so
  it gets `incub = `r params$flu_incub_v2``.

Three fit bands per window, from `r N_REPS` simulations each:

1. **v2**: v2's estimate, every case counted (as in the earlier reports);
2. **`r BAND_ONE`**: the model's estimate with its reporting model;
3. **`r BAND_RANGE`**: parameter draws from the model's range, with its reporting model.

For Utah windows followed by at least 14 days of data, the same simulations run 14 days
further, and those days, which the models did not see, are scored too (a forecast).

```{r real-data}
DD <- params$real_data_dir
covid <- read.csv(file.path(DD, "utah_covid_all_days.csv"))
covid$Date <- as.Date(covid$Date)
hhs <- read.csv(file.path(DD, "utah_hhs_hospital_admissions.csv"))
hhs$date <- as.Date(substr(hhs$date, 1, 10)) - 1   # reported the day after admission
e1918 <- new.env()
load(file.path(DD, "Flu1918.rda"), envir = e1918)

windows <- list()
add_window <- function(dataset, label, x, cases, future, n, disease) {
  windows[[length(windows) + 1]] <<- list(
    dataset = dataset, label = label, x = x, cases = cases, future = future, n = n,
    recov = if (disease == "flu") 0.25 else 1 / 7,
    incub_model = if (disease == "flu") params$flu_incub else params$utah_incub,
    incub_v2 = if (disease == "flu") params$flu_incub_v2 else params$utah_incub
  )
}

utah <- tail(covid, 365)
main_starts <- c(beginning = 1, middle = floor((365 - N_DAYS) / 2) + 1, end = 365 - N_DAYS + 1)
for (s in sort(unique(c(seq(1, 365 - N_DAYS + 1, by = 14), main_starts)))) {
  idx <- s:(s + N_DAYS - 1)
  fut <- if (s + N_DAYS + 13 <= 365) (s + N_DAYS):(s + N_DAYS + 13) else integer(0)
  lab <- if (s %in% main_starts) names(main_starts)[match(s, main_starts)] else ""
  add_window("Utah COVID-19 2024-25", lab, utah$Date[c(idx, fut)], utah$Daily.Cases[idx],
             utah$Daily.Cases[fut], 5000, "COVID-19")
}

peak_window <- function(dataset, x, cases, n, disease) {
  ma  <- as.numeric(stats::filter(cases, rep(1 / 7, 7), sides = 2))
  end <- min(length(cases), which.max(ma) + 7)
  start <- max(1, end - N_DAYS + 1)   # an early peak: the first 61 days
  idx <- start:(start + N_DAYS - 1)
  add_window(dataset, "61 days to a week after the peak", x[idx], cases[idx], numeric(0), n, disease)
}
season <- function(d, y, from, to) list(x = d[d >= as.Date(from) & d <= as.Date(to)],
                                        y = y[d >= as.Date(from) & d <= as.Date(to)])
f1 <- season(hhs$date, hhs$previous_day_admission_influenza_confirmed, "2022-09-01", "2023-05-31")
f2 <- season(hhs$date, hhs$previous_day_admission_influenza_confirmed, "2023-09-01", "2024-04-26")
c3 <- season(covid$Date, covid$Daily.Cases, "2023-06-01", "2023-10-15")
peak_window("Utah flu 2022-23", f1$x, f1$y, 5000, "flu")
peak_window("Utah flu 2023-24", f2$x, f2$y, 5000, "flu")
peak_window("Baltimore flu 1918", seq_along(e1918$Flu1918$incidence), e1918$Flu1918$incidence, 10000, "flu")
peak_window("Utah COVID-19 summer 2023", c3$x, c3$y, 10000, "COVID-19")
cat(length(windows), "windows\n")
```

```{r real-fit}
band <- function(par_rows, ndays) {
  sim  <- seir_simulator(ndays = ndays)
  runs <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(par_rows)), function(i)
    simulate_from_parameters(sim, as.list(par_rows[i, ]), seed = i), numeric(ndays))
  data.frame(median = apply(runs, 1, median),
             lower = apply(runs, 1, quantile, 0.025), upper = apply(runs, 1, quantile, 0.975))
}
# Interval score of the 95% band: its width plus 40 times the distance of each
# observed day outside it (lower is better; a wide band is not rewarded).
score <- function(b, y, days) {
  if (!length(days)) return(c(coverage = NA, MAE = NA, width = NA, interval_score = NA))
  lo <- b$lower[days]; hi <- b$upper[days]
  c(coverage = 100 * mean(y >= lo & y <= hi), MAE = mean(abs(b$median[days] - y)),
    width = mean(hi - lo),
    interval_score = mean((hi - lo) + 40 * pmax(lo - y, 0) + 40 * pmax(y - hi, 0)))
}

set.seed(2026)
fits <- lapply(windows, function(w) {
  k2 <- data.frame(n = w$n, recov = w$recov, incub = w$incub_v2)
  k4 <- data.frame(n = w$n, recov = w$recov, incub = w$incub_model)
  e2 <- predict_models(V2_DIRS, matrix(w$cases, 1), k2)
  e4 <- predict_models(MODEL_DIRS, matrix(w$cases, 1), k4)
  nb <- neighbours(e4, k4)
  ndays <- N_DAYS + length(w$future)
  one <- function(k, e, noise) {
    p <- data.frame(n = k$n, recov = k$recov, incub = k$incub, preval = e$preval, ptran = e$ptran, crate = e$crate)
    if (noise) p <- cbind(p, e[, c("report_rate", "overdispersion", "weekday_sd")])
    p[rep(1, N_REPS), ]
  }
  bands <- setNames(list(
    band(one(k2, e2, FALSE), ndays),
    band(one(k4, e4, TRUE), ndays),
    band(draw_parameters(e4, k4, nb, N_REPS), ndays)
  ), c("v2", BAND_ONE, BAND_RANGE))
  fit_days <- seq_len(N_DAYS)
  fut_days <- N_DAYS + seq_along(w$future)
  metrics <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(bands), function(m) {
    f <- score(bands[[m]], w$cases, fit_days)
    g <- score(bands[[m]], w$future, fut_days)
    data.frame(band = m, coverage_pct = f[["coverage"]], MAE = f[["MAE"]], band_width = f[["width"]],
               interval_score = f[["interval_score"]],
               forecast_coverage_pct = g[["coverage"]], forecast_MAE = g[["MAE"]],
               forecast_interval_score = g[["interval_score"]])
  }))
  list(w = w, e2 = e2, e4 = e4, r0_95 = r0_range(e4, nb, c(0.025, 0.975)), bands = bands, metrics = metrics)
})

real_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(fits, function(f) {
  data.frame(dataset = f$w$dataset, window = f$w$label,
             first_day = format(f$w$x[1]), R0_v2 = f$e2$R0, R0_model = f$e4$R0,
             R0_model_low = f$r0_95[1], R0_model_high = f$r0_95[2],
             reported_share_model = f$e4$report_rate, f$metrics)
}))
write.csv(real_tab, file.path(OUT_DIR, "real_data_fits.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Main windows

```{r real-plots, fig.width=13, fig.height=4.2, results="asis"}
BAND_COLS <- setNames(c("darkorange", "purple", "forestgreen"), c("v2", BAND_ONE, BAND_RANGE))
main <- which(vapply(fits, function(f) nzchar(f$w$label), logical(1)))
for (k in main) {
  f <- fits[[k]]
  cat("\n\n### ", f$w$dataset, ": ", f$w$label, "\n\n", sep = "")
  y_all <- c(f$w$cases, f$w$future)
  ylim  <- range(c(y_all, unlist(lapply(f$bands, function(b) c(b$lower, b$upper)))))
  op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 3.5, 1))
  for (m in names(f$bands)) {
    b <- f$bands[[m]]
    r <- f$metrics[f$metrics$band == m, ]
    x <- f$w$x
    r0 <- if (m == "v2") f$e2$R0 else f$e4$R0
    ttl <- sprintf("%s: R0 %.2f%s\nfit %.0f%%%s", m, r0,
                   if (m == BAND_RANGE) sprintf(" (%.2f-%.2f)", f$r0_95[1], f$r0_95[2]) else "",
                   r$coverage_pct,
                   if (is.na(r$forecast_coverage_pct)) "" else sprintf(" | next 14 days %.0f%%", r$forecast_coverage_pct))
    plot(x, b$median, type = "n", ylim = ylim, xlab = "", ylab = "daily count", main = ttl, cex.main = 0.95)
    if (length(f$w$future)) {
      rect(x[N_DAYS + 1], ylim[1], x[length(x)], ylim[2], col = adjustcolor("grey", 0.25), border = NA)
    }
    polygon(c(x, rev(x)), c(b$upper, rev(b$lower)), col = adjustcolor(BAND_COLS[[m]], 0.3), border = NA)
    lines(x, b$median, col = BAND_COLS[[m]], lwd = 2)
    lines(x, y_all, col = "blue", lwd = 1.5)
    points(x, y_all, col = "blue", pch = 16, cex = 0.4)
  }
  par(op)
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

Grey: the 14 days after the window, not seen by the models. Coverage alone rewards wide
bands, so the tables also give the band width and the **interval score** (the band width
plus 40 times how far each observed day falls outside the band; lower is better).

```{r real-main-table}
knitr::kable(real_tab[real_tab$window != "", c("dataset", "window", "first_day", "band", "R0_v2", "R0_model",
                                                "R0_model_low", "R0_model_high", "coverage_pct", "band_width",
                                                "interval_score", "forecast_coverage_pct")],
             digits = 2, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r seeds}
seed_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(SEEDS), function(k) {

  data.frame(model = paste("seed", SEEDS[k]), R0_MAE_new_test_bank = mean(abs(e$R0 - test_bank$theta$R0)))
}))
```

# Summary

```{r summary}
other_real <- real_tab[real_tab$dataset != "Utah COVID-19 2024-25", ]
summary_tab <- rbind(
  data.frame(measure = c("R0 MAE, new test bank (reported cases)", "R0 MAE, v2's test bank (every case)"),
             v2 = test_tab$v2_R0_MAE[c(1, 4)], model = test_tab$model_R0_MAE[c(1, 4)], model_with_range = NA),
  data.frame(measure = "True R0 inside the 95% range (%)", v2 = NA, model = NA,
             model_with_range = range_tab$in_95_range_pct[1]),
  do.call(rbind, lapply(list(
    list("Utah COVID 2024-25, fit coverage (mean of windows, %)", "mean_fit_coverage_pct"),
    list("Utah COVID 2024-25, fit interval score (lower is better)", "mean_fit_interval_score"),
    list("Utah COVID 2024-25, next-14-day coverage (mean, %)", "mean_forecast_coverage_pct"),
    list("Utah COVID 2024-25, next-14-day interval score (lower is better)", "mean_forecast_interval_score")),
    function(r) {
      v <- setNames(utah_summary[[r[[2]]]], utah_summary$band)
      data.frame(measure = r[[1]], v2 = v[["v2"]], model = v[[BAND_ONE]], model_with_range = v[[BAND_RANGE]])
    })),
  do.call(rbind, lapply(unique(other_real$dataset), function(d) {
    labels <- c(coverage_pct = "fit coverage (%)", interval_score = "fit interval score")
    do.call(rbind, lapply(names(labels), function(col) {
      s <- other_real$dataset == d
      v <- setNames(other_real[[col]][s], other_real$band[s])
      data.frame(measure = paste0(d, ", ", labels[[col]]),
                 v2 = v[["v2"]], model = v[[BAND_ONE]], model_with_range = v[[BAND_RANGE]])
    }))
  }))
)
write.csv(summary_tab, file.path(OUT_DIR, "summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(summary_tab, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```
